changedBeliefs: After [exp 195](195-stmt-cache-name-tokens.md) cached the column-name tokens on the prepared-statement entry and [exp 198](198-direct-buf-int-float-json.md) collapsed the per-cell integer/float formatter to a direct write, the inner per-cell loop of `write_json_to_buf` still paid one `buf_ensure` per token write and one per cell value — roughly `2N + 2` ensures per N-column row. Hoisting them all into a single row-level `buf_ensure(prelude + tokens_total + col_count * (RESQLITE_JSON_FLOAT_MAX + 1) + 1)` and writing NULL / INTEGER / FLOAT cells directly to `b->data + b->len` removes the per-cell ensures without changing the output. TEXT / BLOB cells take the existing helpers and pay one extra `buf_ensure(remaining_tokens + remaining_cells + 1)` after each variable-cell call, which exactly offsets the per-cell ensure they would have used.

Two order-flipped focused passes on `select_bytes_int_heavy.dart` reproduce the win same-direction on all five integer-heavy lanes: 10k × 8 small ints −1.6 % / −4.0 %, 10k × 20 small ints −6.8 % / −2.8 %, 10k × 20 big ints −1.7 % / −3.0 %, mixed-row (4 int + 2 text + 2 real) −0.6 % / −0.6 %, 1k × 2 ints −3.8 % / −1.9 %. The magnitude is smaller than exp 192 / exp 198 (−7 % to −9 % on the same lanes) because what is left after exp 198 is the per-cell ensure branch itself — one predicted comparison — not a multi-byte memcpy or formatter call.

`select_bytes_real_int_fastpath.dart` lanes all stay inside ±1 %: the integer-via-REAL fast path already wrote directly through exp 198, so this hoist saves only the per-cell ensure branch for it, and `fast_double_to_json_num`'s `snprintf("%.17g")` dwarfs that on the fractional-REAL path. `select_bytes_wide_cols.dart` int-only lanes (10k × 8 and 10k × 20) reproduce the focused win at −3.8 % / −2.4 %; mixed lanes neutral; sub-millisecond regression guards (1-row / 100-row) live below the harness resolution and are not load-bearing.
nextSignals: The natural next encoder candidate is a prepared-statement type cache that skips per-row `sqlite3_column_type` for stable-typed queries, but SQLite type affinity can vary per row and the audit cost is real — defer until a workload shows column_type as a measurable fraction of selectBytes wall.

The fractional REAL path remains dominated by `snprintf("%.17g")`; a hand-rolled Grisu2 / Ryu replacement is the next bounded candidate against that, requires an output-equivalence audit against snprintf, and is the largest remaining per-cell saving in `write_json_to_buf` after this experiment.

Any future encoder change inside `write_json_to_buf` should keep the row-level reservation pattern intact: pre-reserve at row start, write fixed cells directly, re-ensure after TEXT / BLOB. The TEXT / BLOB recovery path is a single ensure call per variable-size cell and is the right baseline cost for mixed-row workloads.
